title: Skyrim Explained | The Dragonborn, Shouts, DLC, Mods And Sales | Gaming Explained
description: Skyrim explained: the 2011 release, the land of Skyrim, the Dragonborn and dragon shouts, three expansions, mods, re-releases and sales passing sixty million.
joke: In Skyrim the dragons are scary, but the real danger is a chicken when you accidentally hit it.

sections.heading: A game that never left
sections.script: Welcome back to the channel. Today we are explaining The Elder Scrolls five: Skyrim, the fantasy role playing game that has stayed popular for well over a decade. It first arrived on November eleventh, twenty eleven, and people are still starting new characters today. We will look at what Skyrim is, where and when it is set, who you play, what dragon shouts are, how the open world works, what the three big expansions added, and why the game has been released again and again on new platforms. We will also talk about mods, the sales numbers, and why so many players call it a comfort game. Our facts come from Wikipedia, from Bethesda's own pages, and from news coverage of the releases. Let us begin.

sections.heading: What Skyrim is
sections.script: The Elder Scrolls five: Skyrim is an action role playing game developed by Bethesda Game Studios and published by Bethesda Softworks. Todd Howard directed it. It is the fifth main game in The Elder Scrolls series, following Oblivion, and it launched in twenty eleven for Windows, the PlayStation three and the Xbox three sixty. Unlike many games that guide you down a single path, Skyrim drops you into a huge world and lets you decide what to do first. You can follow the main story, join guilds, explore ruins, or simply wander the mountains and see what you find. That freedom is the core idea of the game, and it is the main reason people still return to it. There is no timer pushing you forward, so every player ends up with a slightly different story to tell.

sections.heading: The land of Skyrim
sections.script: The game is set in Skyrim, the northern province of the continent of Tamriel. It is a cold land of snowy mountains, pine forests, frozen coasts and old stone ruins. Bethesda's own description of the game mentions Blackreach, a vast underground region full of glowing mushrooms, and it places Skyrim inside the wider Empire of Tamriel. According to Wikipedia, the story takes place two hundred and one years after Oblivion. The team chose a largely sub arctic setting instead of the lush Cyrodiil used in the previous game, which gave Skyrim a very different mood. Cities such as Whiterun and Windhelm, with their wooden halls and stone walls, feel like real places with their own people and problems.

sections.heading: The Dragonborn
sections.script: In Skyrim you play as the Dragonborn, called the Dovahkiin in the dragon language. Bethesda describes this hero as a prophesied figure with the body of a mortal and the soul of a dragon. The main story begins when dragons return to the land, and Wikipedia says the player must stop Alduin the World-Eater, a dragon destined to destroy the world. You create your own character, choosing a race and a look, and then decide how to play. Warrior, thief, mage or something in between, the game never locks you into a class. You improve skills simply by using them, so a character who swings swords gets better at swords, and one who casts spells becomes a stronger mage over time.

sections.heading: Dragons and shouts
sections.script: The most famous feature of the game is the dragon shout. As the Dragonborn, you can absorb the souls of dragons you defeat, and these souls let you learn Thu'um, or shouts, built from words in the dragon language. Bethesda says the shouts add a third method of attack or defense next to weapons and magic. Some shouts push enemies away, some slow down time, and some call allies. The game's main theme, called Dragonborn, is sung in that fictional language, and it has become one of the best known pieces of music in modern gaming. Seeing a dragon appear over a village while you are walking to a quest is a moment that many players remember very clearly, and learning a new shout for the first time feels like a real reward for exploring.

sections.heading: A world that lives
sections.script: One reason Skyrim feels alive is that the world keeps moving without you. Bethesda's article about the game describes characters and creatures that live their lives on their own, with wolves hunting deer and dragons attacking settlements. Wikipedia explains that this relies on an updated version of the Radiant AI system first built for Oblivion, which lets characters farm, mine and react to events. This means the world does not simply wait for you to arrive, and a trip across the map can turn into an adventure you never planned. Together these systems create small stories you can tell your friends, such as a surprise dragon attack on a quiet road that you had to survive with only a few potions and a rusty sword.

sections.heading: Dawnguard, Hearthfire and Dragonborn
sections.script: Skyrim also received three large add ons. Dawnguard added vampires and crossbows, and a conflict between two factions. Hearthfire let you build and furnish houses and even adopt children. Dragonborn took players to the island of Solstheim, with new quests and the chance to ride dragons. All three are named by both Wikipedia and Bethesda, and all three are included in the later Special Edition. These expansions did more than add content, because they changed how players used the main game. Some people spent hundreds of hours building a home, while others focused on becoming the most powerful vampire hunter in the land. The base game was big enough that adding more simply gave everyone a new way to play.

sections.heading: Mods keep it fresh
sections.script: Another big reason Skyrim stays popular is modding. Players can use the Creation Kit to build their own changes, and mods are shared through sites such as Nexus Mods and the Steam Workshop, according to Wikipedia. Mods can add new weapons, better graphics, new quests, or even full games. Wikipedia mentions Enderal and The Forgotten City as well known examples that started as mods. Bethesda also launched Creation Club, a collection of paid content packs, and the Anniversary Edition later bundled seventy four of those creations. Mods mean the game never feels finished, and they give long time players a reason to start again with a completely different set of rules.

sections.heading: Re-releases and sales
sections.script: Skyrim has been released many times. The Special Edition arrived in October twenty sixteen with improved visuals and all three expansions, and the Anniversary Edition came on November eleventh, twenty twenty one, to mark ten years. Coverage of that release noted it bundled the game, its expansions and Creation Club content. The Nintendo Switch also received a version, and there is a virtual reality edition too. Bethesda said in twenty sixteen that the game had sold thirty million copies, and in twenty twenty three Todd Howard told IGN that it had passed sixty million across several console generations. That puts Skyrim among the best selling video games ever made, and it shows how strongly players have kept coming back to this snowy corner of Tamriel year after year, across console generations and computers.

sections.heading: Your Skyrim story
sections.script: That is Skyrim explained: a northern land of mountains and ruins, a hero with a dragon soul, shouts that shake the sky, expansions that added vampires and houses, and a mod scene that keeps it fresh. Whether you started on the Xbox three sixty in twenty eleven or on a modern console years later, the game offers a story that feels like yours. We are curious about how you played it. Did you become a mighty warrior, a sneaky thief or a powerful mage, and what was your favourite quest or moment? Tell us in the comments below.
